groupDistance.basis: Every member sits at the cluster's distance, Baumgardt & Vasiliev's (2021) 8.90 kpc for NGC 6637 (the query writes it into each row), spread in depth as widely as the members spread across the sky: that the cluster is as deep as it is wide is an assumption, not a measurement of any member's depth. A member's own parallax at this distance measures less than its place in the cluster.

sample: The 318 stars Hunt & Reffert (2023, A&A 673, A114) list as members of NGC_6637 within its tidal radius (inrt = True, their own selection of reliable members), of 445 members in all, that have a Gaia DR3 G magnitude and BP-RP color; 0 within the tidal radius without a color are left out. Gaia misses stars in the crowded core, so the centre of a globular cluster is thinner here than in the sky.
meaning: Member stars of M69 from Hunt & Reffert's (2023) Gaia DR3 cluster census, one dot per star at its measured sky position, at the cluster's distance. Drawn when the cluster is selected.

colorByBpRp.basis: Measured Gaia DR3 BP-RP, as observed (not corrected for the dust in front of the cluster), through Cardiel et al.'s (2021) RGB fit, as the nebula star fields color Gaia stars. A color beyond the range takes its end.

toneBy.basis: A display scale: each member's G magnitude minus the distance modulus of the cluster's distance darkens its color, from full at -3 to 45% at +6, linear in magnitude; the dot size and the faintest tone are the nuclear star cluster's. Dust in front of the cluster (Hunt & Reffert's A_V 2.14 mag) is not removed.

fullDetail.basis: Presentation choice: whole within 27 kpc of the Sun, three times the cluster's distance, so every member shows while the cluster is selected and framed (the bank's origin is the Sun; the renderer's default of 10 kpc is nearer than three times this cluster).
